 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 24-09-2023 at about 5.00 a.m., the petitioner was traveling in a Bolero Maxi truck vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP- 03-TK-4992 from their village to Santhipuram village, on Kuppam-Palamaner NH-42 road along with his villagers.
The driver by name M. Damodharam was driving the bolero maxi truck vehicle by following all the traffic rules, on the extreme left side of the road, slowly and cautiously.

While they were proceeding near Veeraraju Nursery, near Devadoddi Village, Baireddypalle Mandalam, Palamaner Taluk, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, at that time the driver of Mercedes Benz car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369 came from opposite direction i.e. towards Baireddypalle side, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life and violently dashed against the Bolero Maxi truck vehicle of the petitioner.

Due to the said impact, the petitioner, Reddappa and M.
Damodaram
sustained grievous injuries and the bolero vehicle was also fully damaged.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Palamaner, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Vishwakirana Hospital, Madanapalle, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was doing agriculture and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Baireddypalle Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, the accident occurred due to the fault of the petitioner.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner at the time of accident handled his Bolero Maxi Truck vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TK-4992 in a negligent manner, as the said bolero maxi truck was unlawfully loaded with maximum number of cattle's (i.e. cows), which has led to the accident.
However, after the said accident the petitioner using the local influence has lodged a false complaint against the Mercedes Benz car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369, in Baireddypalle Police Station.
The petitioner himself was sole and exclusive cause for the alleged accident.
There was absolutely no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of Mercedes Benz car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the p e t i t i o n . I t h a s a d m i t t e d t h e i s s u a n c e o f p r i v a t e c a r p a c k a g e p o l i c y b e a r i n g No.1702003123P100960283, in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of car bearing No.TN-07-BX-9369 and its validity from 27-04-2023 to 26-04-2024.

Further it is contended that,
the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him.

Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of the alleged accident and the respondent No.1 knowingly and willfully entrusted his vehicle to such a person.
Hence, there is express breach of driver's clause, absolving the insurer from any liability.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the alleged accident occurred only on account of the carelessness on the part of the driver of the Mahindra Bolero bearing No.AP-03- TK-4992, the said vehicle driver drove the same without having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same,
without observing vehicle movements and driving the vehicle in a zig zag manner and came towards the wrong side and dashed against the insured car.
Hence, compensation if any awardable to the petitioner is to be reduced by 75%.

Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary party as the insurer and owner of the vehicle bearing No.AP-03-TK-4992, as they are not made party to the present proceedings.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:

2.

7. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 10 documents as Ex.P.1 to 10.
On the other hand, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material available on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:

REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 24-09-2023 at about 5.00 a.m., when he was traveling in a Bolero Maxi truck vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TK-4992 from their village to Santhipuram village, on Kuppam- Palamaner NH-42 road along with his villagers and when they were near Veeraraju Nursery, near Devadoddi Village, Baireddypalle Mandalam, Palamaner Taluk,
Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, at that the driver of offending Mercedes Benz car bearing Reg.
No.TN-07-BX-9369 came from opposite side i.e. towards Baireddypalle side, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Bolero vehicle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was doing agriculture and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 10 documents as Ex.P.1 to 10.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 are medical bills, Ex.P.2 is notarized copy of Aadhar card,
Ex.P.3 is MRI scan report, Ex.P.4 are MRI scan films, Ex.P.5 are x- rays, Ex.P.6 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.8 and 8(a) are true copy of first information statement and its translated copy, Ex.P.9 and 9(a) are true copy of sketch and its translated copy and Ex.P.10 is true copy of charge-sheet.
12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.6 to 10, prima-facia

it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369 and dashing the same against the Bolero Krishnababu .K vs Karthik A on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105097719/
4 Maxi Truck vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TK-4992 from opposite direction, in which the petitioners and others were traveling.
Due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.10, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TK- 4992 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg.
No.TN-07-BX-9369.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the police authorities and owner of Bolero Maxi Truck vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TK-4992 has got registered a false case against the driver of car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369, to get wrongful gain from the respondents.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence, nor they have produced any document to show that, at the relevant point of time of accident the driver of Bolero Mxi Truck was driving his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and the accident in question has occurred solely due to his rash and negligent driving.
Even the respondents have not stepped into witness box to depose the above contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN- 07-BX-9369 and dashing the same against the Bolero Maxi Truck vehicle bearing No.AP-03-TK-4992 from opposite direction.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck vehicle bearing No.AP-03-TK-4992 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.9 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of Kuppam- Palamaner NH-42 road, near Veeraraju Nursery, at Devadoddi Village,
Baireddipalli Mandalam, Palamaner Taluk, Chittor District, Andhra Pradesh, in between offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369 and oncoming Bolero Maxi Truck vehicle bearing Reg.
No.AP-03- TK-4992.
Further, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck vehicle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report,
marked as Ex.P.10, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such Krishnababu .K vs Karthik A on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105097719/
5 circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

sentences.text: 15. No doubt, there is a delay of one day in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.8 first information statement.
He has clearly stated that, after undergoing treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident he went to the Police Station and lodged the complaint.
Hence, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

entities.text: Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."
16. There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above stated reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision and taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that, the delay in lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

17. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.3 MRI scan report, Ex.P.4 MRI scan films,
Ex.P.5 x-rays and Ex.P.6 wound certificate it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained fracture of lateral spinous process of scapula with adjacent posterior deltoid muscle plane of subcutaneous edema.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the said medical records of the petitioner.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.

18. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held

20. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 24-09-2023 at about 5.00 a.m., on Kuppam-Palamaner NH-42 road, near Veeraraju Nursery, at Devadoddi Village,
Baireddipalli Mandalam, Palamaner Taluk, Chittor District, Andhra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Mercedes Benz Car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX- 9369.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Mercedes Benz Car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX- 9369 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of lateral spinous process of scapula with adjacent posterior deltoid muscle plane of subcutaneous edema and for the said injuries he has undergone conservative treatment.

Therefore,
this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
But, there is no evidence placed on record by the petitioner for the purpose of assessing the above pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

In such circumstances,
there is no other option before this Court, except to consider global compensation in general.
22. As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained abrasion over the left shoulder and abrasion over the left leg.
The MRI report shows fracture of lateral spinous process of scapula with adjacent posterior deltoid muscle plane of subcutaneous edema.
Further, the petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 8 medical bills, as per Ex.P.1.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the bills at Sl No.1 to 5, 7 and 8 are not in the name of the petitioner.
Therefore, the said bills are not taken into consideration.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards the medical expenses.
23. Further, the petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, earlier to the accident he was working as agriculturist and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
But, he has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.

Further, he has neither examined any doctor, nor he has produced any document to show that, due to injuries sustained in the said accident he has suffered any permanent physical disability or deformity and thereby he has lost his earning capacity or he is not in a position to perform his day to day activities.
Such being the case, it is difficult to ascertain pain and sufferings, loss of income during the laid off period, loss of amenities etc.

But,
due to above injuries definitely the petitioner would have suffered some pain and sufferings and the same would have been nourished with nutritious food and he might have attended with the attendants during the treatment period.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into Krishnababu .K vs Karthik A on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105097719/
7 consideration the age of the petitioner, the nature of injuries sustained, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for some reasonable compensation.

sentences.text: As such, awarding global compensation of Rs.55,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, to the petitioner, would be just, fair and reasonable compensation and it would meet the ends of justice.
24. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX- 9369.
As per insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 vide policy bearing No.1702003123P100960283, in respect of offending car, was valid from 27-04-2023 to 26- 04-2024.

As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e.
24-09-2023.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.55,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.55,000/- (Rupees fifty five thousand only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment, on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Hence, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
16. There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above stated reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision and taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that, the delay in lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.
The petitioner has sustained fracture of lateral spinous process of scapula with adjacent posterior deltoid muscle plane of subcutaneous edema.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the said medical records of the petitioner.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-07-BX-9369 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
18. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards the medical expenses.
